But it never lasted more than a few days, a week at most, and it wasn't like a full-blown episode where things got out of control or really messed with my life. It just felt like a brief, intense burst of energy before I’d crash right back into this familiar gloom. It’s like those energized moments weren’t even real, or they didn’t quite get to the point where I completely lost touch with reality or caused problems.

I feel so flat, like my emotions are stuck in neutral; happy things don't really lift me, and sad things don't really sting. At work, on the crane, I used to feel pride, but now I just feel… less than. I look at the other operators and feel like I'm always messing up, not as good as them. D014-D009_h006.question_b:

D014-D009_h015.question_both: Honestly, doc, it’s been about two and a half years now, this feeling. Some days I just wake up and it’s like a dark cloud has already settled. I run the bakery, you know, my late husband’s dream, and I just can’t seem to shake this feeling that everything’s going to go wrong. D014-D009_h015.question_a:
It's been almost two and a half years now, maybe even longer, since I’ve really felt like myself. Waking up each morning leaves me feeling just as tired as when I went to bed, even if I’ve had a full eight hours. Running the bakery used to be my joy, but lately, everything just feels so bleak. I can’t help but see the worst in every situation; a new order comes in, and my first thought is what could go wrong. It’s hard not to just burst into tears sometimes, even over small things, and I often find myself crying alone in the back room.

There have been times – fleeting moments, really – when I’ve felt a burst of energy, almost like my old self again, staying up late to bake or meticulously planning new recipes. But these never last long, and they’re certainly not what I’d call a "high." They don't have that frantic, out-of-control feeling people describe, and I’ve never experienced anything like that before. After those brief spurts, I just crash back into this heavy sadness. It's really taking a toll on my ability to manage the bakery and enjoy time with my grandchildren.

I cry easily these days; sometimes just seeing an old couple happy together sets me off. And I never feel rested, no matter how long I stay in bed. Everything just feels… bleak. I can’t see things getting better.

The strange thing is, there have been these odd stretches, maybe a few days at a time, where it’s like a different person takes over. I get this amazing burst of energy, I barely need sleep, and my mind races with so many ideas for the bakery – I even tried to redecorate the whole shop by myself last spring, staying up all night for three days straight. My daughter thought I was crazy, but I felt so productive, so brilliant! Then, just as suddenly, I’d crash back down into this exhaustion and gloom. But mostly, it’s just this dragging sadness."
